name: Create Order
overview: An order is how you schedule pickups and deliveries of linen items for your customers. Each order belongs to a customer and specifies when items are picked up and delivered.

fields.label: Order Reference ID
fields.explanation: This is a unique identifier for your order. You can enter a custom reference like 'ORD-2026-001' to easily track and search for this order later. If you leave it blank, the system will auto-generate one when you save.
fields.tips: Use a consistent naming pattern like ORD-YYYY-NNN so your team can quickly identify orders.

commonQuestions.question: What happens if I leave this blank?
commonQuestions.answer: The system will auto-generate a reference ID when you save the order.

commonQuestions.question: Can I use any format?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes, you can use any format. But a consistent pattern like ORD-YYYY-NNN makes orders easier to find.

fields.label: Customer
fields.explanation: This is the customer who is placing the order. Start typing the customer name and the system will search automatically. Only active customers will appear in the results.
fields.tips: If a customer doesn't show up, check if they are marked as active in the Customers section.

commonQuestions.question: Why can't I find my customer?
commonQuestions.answer: Only active customers appear in the search. Check the Customers page to make sure the customer is active and not deactivated.

commonQuestions.question: Can I create a new customer from here?
commonQuestions.answer: No, you need to create the customer first from the Customers page, then come back to create the order.

fields.label: Order Date
fields.explanation: This is the date the order is being created. It defaults to today's date. Changing this will automatically adjust the pickup and delivery dates to maintain the same gap.
fields.tips: If you set this to a past date, the pickup and delivery dates will shift accordingly. This is useful for backdating orders.

commonQuestions.question: Can I set a past date?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes, you can set a past order date. The pickup and delivery dates will adjust to maintain the same number of days between them.

fields.label: Order Type
fields.explanation: This determines what kind of order this is. Leasing means you are renting linen items to the customer. Rental is for short-term use. Washing means the customer is sending items for laundry service. The type you choose changes which fields appear below.
fields.tips: Most orders in this system are Leasing orders. Only choose Rental or Washing if your business specifically uses those workflows.

commonQuestions.question: What is the difference between Leasing and Rental?
commonQuestions.answer: Leasing is for long-term linen contracts where items are delivered and picked up on a schedule. Rental is short-term, like an event or a one-time use.

commonQuestions.question: What does Washing mean?
commonQuestions.answer: A Washing order is when the customer sends their own linen to your facility for cleaning. You pick it up, wash it, and deliver it back.

fields.label: Adjustment Order
fields.explanation: Turn this on if this order is an adjustment to a previous order. Adjustment orders are used to correct quantities, add missing items, or make changes to an existing order without creating a brand new one.
fields.tips: Only use this when correcting a previous order. New orders should have this turned off.

commonQuestions.question: When should I use Adjustment Order?
commonQuestions.answer: Use it when you need to correct or modify an existing order, like adding items that were missed or adjusting quantities.

fields.label: Delivery Type
fields.explanation: This controls whether this order includes a delivery, a pickup, or both. Delivery means you bring items to the customer. Pickup means you collect items from the customer. Both means you do both — deliver fresh items and collect used ones.
fields.tips: Most Leasing orders use 'Both' because you deliver fresh linen and pick up the used ones in the same trip.

commonQuestions.question: What if I only need to pick up items?
commonQuestions.answer: Choose 'Pickup' and the system will only show pickup-related fields and items.

fields.label: Pickup Date
fields.explanation: This is the date when your team will go to the customer's location to collect used linen items. It defaults to one day after the order date.
fields.tips: Make sure pickup dates don't fall on weekends or holidays unless your team operates on those days.

commonQuestions.question: Can the pickup date be before the order date?
commonQuestions.answer: Technically yes, but it's unusual. The system allows it for edge cases like backdating.

fields.label: Delivery Date
fields.explanation: This is the date when your team will deliver fresh linen items to the customer's location. It defaults to one day after the order date.
fields.tips: Delivery dates should account for processing time. Make sure your warehouse has enough stock to fulfill the order by this date.

commonQuestions.question: What if delivery is delayed?
commonQuestions.answer: You can edit the order later to change the delivery date. The system does not automatically reschedule.

subForms.name: Delivery Item

autoPopulatedTrigger.description: Products auto-populate based on the customer's reserved products after selection

fallbackManual.description: Click this if no products auto-populate for the selected customer

subForms.explanationForMultiple: You can add multiple items to a single order. Let me add a second one to show you.
subForms.explanation: Now we add the actual items to be delivered to the customer. These are the linen products they will receive.

fields.label: Product
fields.explanation: Select the linen product being delivered. The list shows products that are reserved for this customer in their agreement. If the customer has reserved products, this field is automatically filled for you.

fields.label: Quantity
fields.explanation: Enter the number of items to deliver. This should match what the customer needs for this delivery cycle.

fields.label: Remarks
fields.explanation: Add any special instructions about this item. For example, 'Premium quality required' or 'Handle with care'.

subForms.name: Pickup Item
subForms.explanationForMultiple: Let me add a second pickup item to show you.
subForms.explanation: These are the items being picked up from the customer. You can add them manually, or use the 'Use same items as Delivery' checkbox to copy the delivery items automatically.

fields.label: Product
fields.explanation: Select the linen product being picked up from the customer. This should match the type of items that were originally delivered to them.

fields.label: Quantity
fields.explanation: Enter the number of items being picked up. This may differ from the delivery quantity if some items are still in use at the customer's location.

fields.label: Remarks
fields.explanation: Add any notes about the pickup. For example, 'Customer reported 5 damaged items' or 'Partial pickup requested'.

subForms.name: Rental Item
subForms.explanation: Add the linen items the customer is renting. Rental orders are for short-term use, like events or temporary setups.

fields.label: Product
fields.explanation: Select the linen product being rented out to the customer. The available products come from your product catalog.

fields.label: Quantity
fields.explanation: Enter the number of items being rented. Make sure this matches what was agreed with the customer.

fields.label: Rental Duration (days)
fields.explanation: Enter how many days the customer will be renting these items. This affects the billing calculation — longer durations cost more.

subForms.name: Washing Item
subForms.explanation: Add the linen items being sent for washing. Washing orders are for customers who want their own linen cleaned at your facility.

fields.label: Product
fields.explanation: Select the linen product being sent for washing. This is the type of item the customer wants cleaned.

fields.label: Quantity
fields.explanation: Enter the number of items being sent for laundry service. The total will be used to calculate the washing charges.

wrapUp: That covers all the fields for creating an order! You've seen how to select a customer, choose the order type, set dates, and add items. Remember, this was a demo — all the data has been cleared. When you're ready, you can create a real order. Just say the name of any other form if you'd like to learn about it.
